ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, this is the creative physics experiment design work “Little Bear Swinging on a Swing.” Two metal rods C and D that are close to each other and insulated from each other are fixed on an iron stand, and form a closed circuit with two copper coils P and Q. Two very strongly magnetic bar magnets are placed as shown in the figure. When coil P is swung left and right by hand, coil Q also swings along with it, as if the little bear is swinging on a swing. Which of the following statements is correct? (　　)

Two metal rods C and D, close to each other and mutually insulated, are fixed on an iron stand and form a closed loop with two copper coils P and Q. Two very strong bar magnets are placed as shown in the figure. During the process in which coil P swings to the right, what is the direction of the current in coil P (viewed from right to left)?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The figure shows the creative physics experiment design work "Little Bear Swinging on a Swing." Two metal rods C and D, close to each other and mutually insulated, are fixed on an iron stand and form a closed loop with two copper coils P and Q. Two very strong bar magnets are placed as shown in the figure. During the process in which coil P swings to the right, what is the direction of the current in coil P (viewed from right to left)?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the lower left of the figure there is a horizontally placed bar magnet, the end close to coil P is marked "S", and coil P is drawn on the right side of this S pole and connected with the two metal rods C and D close to each other above to form a loop; on the right side there is also coil Q and another magnet marked "S", but this question only determines the direction of the current in P. The problem states that coil P swings to the right, so P gradually moves away from the S pole of the left magnet. Then reason: Outside the magnet, magnetic field lines enter the S pole, so the magnetic field passing through the coil at P points toward the left S pole, that is, to the left. When P moves right away from the S pole, the leftward magnetic flux through coil P decreases. According to Lenz's law, the magnetic field produced by the induced current in P should hinder this decrease, so the induced magnetic field should also be to the left. When viewing coil P from right to left, a leftward magnetic field is in the direction away from the observer, pointing into the paper; by the right-hand screw rule, the current direction producing this magnetic field is clockwise.
